newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge condemns Phnom Penh grenade attack.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge condemns Phnom Penh grenade attack.

text.p: The Khmer Rouge guerrilla movement on Monday condemned a deadly grenade attack on opposition demonstrators in Phnom Penh at the weekend which killed at least 12 and blamed it on co-Premier Hun Sen.

A Khmer Rouge spokesman said on the guerrillas' clandestine radio that the group "would like to comdemn severely" the attack on a protest led by opposition leader Sam Rainsy, which also injured more than 100 people.

The Khmer Rouge spokesman blamed Hun Sen for the attack and said it was aimed at "destroying" Sam Rainsy, his Khmer Nation Party (KNP) and his political alliance with co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh.

Phnom Penh police said four grenades exploded on Sunday morning in a crowd of up to 200 people demonstrating outside the National Assembly building in central Phnom Penh. The protest was organised by Sam Rainsy against what he termed subservience of the judiciary to Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party.
Sam Rainsy, who narrowly escaped injury in the attack, also blamed it on Hun Sen.
The Khmer Rouge, which led the brutal 1975-1979 "killing fields" regime, has expressed support for Ranariddh and Sam Rainsy's recently formed alliance, the National United Front.

The Maoist guerillas, under whose rule more than one million Cambodians died from overwork, starvation, execution, and disease, signed a U.N.-sponsored peace pact in 1991 but later reneged on the deal and have been fighting the coalition government formed after the 1993 polls.
They have been hit by defections over the past year, with fewer than 2,000 of the hardline rebels remaining. These guerillas based in the northwest are in talks with the government.

Sam Rainsy became a leading opposition figure after being fired as finance minister in 1994. He was expelled from parliament in 1995 and his party is not recognised by the current coalition government.
